findings.claim: reserve-flow D1 shows the confirmation at GET /reserved/<id> "while the book is held" and does not tie it to the form token or claim, so a neighbour whose hold has lapsed, or anyone else who opens that address, is shown the confirmation for a hold another neighbour now has, which cuts against V-7 ("never promised to two neighbours at once"), and no acceptance clause tests it.

I-2's witness would pass with the reserved mark gone: floor.test.js checks the reserved book's list item against /reserved/i, and the fixture's title "Marked Reserved Title" always matches, so only the unlisted test at test/shelf.test.js line 33 catches a missing mark, and reserve-flow is the unit that changes this code.

keeper-cli D2 has list word a hold end with holdEndWords from the stored reservedUntil and design-keeper A3 has list show "until when", but b2 in the seed data has reservedBy and no reservedUntil, store-update A5 keeps such a book held, and no spec says what list prints for it or what holdEndWords does with a missing end, so the seed shelf's first list hits an undefined case.

reasons: Both earlier blocking findings are resolved, and this review adds no blocking finding, so no blocking finding holds the first admission.

review-1#0 is resolved: window-rule A3 now words a hold end from the stored instant alone, reserve-flow D2 words every confirmation from the stored reservedUntil, and keeper-cli D2 does the same for list without reading a settings file.
review-1#1 is resolved: the census now marks T-29 as obligation I-36, I-36 serves V-11, and page-access A4 and W-1 give it a witness that a lane can run against the served stylesheet.
I checked every census entry against its obligation's rule: all 36 active rules are present, each maps to the obligation anchored at it, and each obligation's statement restates its rule's text.

I checked each clause the slice advances against the serves lists: V-1, V-2, V-3, V-5 to V-13 are each served by at least one obligation, although V-10 is served only by I-5, which review-1#14 already covers.

I compared the rev 1 and rev 2 specs. The acceptance clauses of keeper-cli and settings-file did not change, keeper-cli D2 gained only the holdEndWords wording, and the only spec text change in page-access is A4 plus its witness.
The earlier findings on store-update, design-page, design-keeper, the plan and the Phase-0 record stay open because none of those files changed, and the changes to other specs do not settle them.

The earlier notes on keeper-cli, settings-file, reserve-flow and page-access stay open because their current text still has the gap: no clock seam for the command or the spawned server, no outcome for a missing SWAPSHELF_CONFIG file, the open flow decisions, the unconditional nextId default and no lane proof for V-10.
The date facts hold: 25 October 2026 and 8 November 2026 are Sundays, and TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati with TZ=Etc/GMT+12 does catch a UTC slip at any hour, as keeper-cli A2 claims.
The palette contrast figures in the specs hold on a recalculation from public/style.css: soft ink about 5.3:1 and rust about 6.3:1 on the paper colour.
I did not run the test suite or any product code, because this review is read-only.

premises.claim: The T-2 test's fixture title for the reserved book contains the word Reserved, and the test's positive check is a case-insensitive match for reserved on that book's list item.
Book b2 in the seed data has reservedBy Priya and no reservedUntil field.
The served stylesheet already defines the paper, ink, rust and hand-lettering values that page-access A4 keeps, and h1 and h2 use the lettering family.
createApp takes only dataPath today and the server entry point exposes no clock.
The keeper corpus states that the commands run on the box over ssh and that a settings change reaches the page when the server next starts.
The orchestrator config already sets chain.k to 1.
The .gitignore covers *.tmp, as store-update D1 relies on for the lock file.
